Exercise book prices to fall by 18% from December 1

cards.what_happened: The National Book Traders' Association announced that retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. It says the nationwide reduction is a direct result of VAT exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget.
details: The National Book Traders' Association has announced that the retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. The price reduction applies nationwide.

The association says the nationwide reduction comes as a direct result of the Value Added Tax (VAT) exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget. The announcement was reported by Newswire.
key_facts: National Book Traders' Association announced an 18% cut in retail prices of all exercise books.
The price reduction starts December 1 and applies across the island.
The cut is a direct result of VAT exemptions and concessions.
Those VAT exemptions and concessions are proposed under the 2027 National Budget.
The announcement was reported by Newswire.
cards.whats_next: Exercise book retail prices will be reduced by 18% starting December 1.
cards.blurb: Exercise books will cost 18% less from December 1, after VAT exemptions and concessions in the 2027 National Budget.
cards.spoken: Good evening. If you buy exercise books, there is some news for you. The National Book Traders' Association has announced that the retail prices of all exercise books across the island will be reduced by 18% starting December 1. That is a nationwide price reduction. The association says this cut comes as a direct result of the Value Added Tax, or VAT, exemptions and concessions proposed under the 2027 National Budget. So from December 1, every exercise book sold across the island will carry a price that is 18% lower. That is the announcement from the National Book Traders' Association, reported by Newswire.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts two missiles, two drones in Riyadh

cards.what_happened: Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted two ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh early Sunday, following the interception of two drones in Riyadh and southern regions on Saturday. The coalition also intercepted several drones aimed at Yemen's Marib city. Fighting intensified across multiple Yemeni governorates with heavy casualties and displacements reported.
details: On Sunday, coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki posted on X that air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward Riyadh. On Saturday, al-Maliki said two suspected Houthi drones were intercepted and destroyed in the Riyadh and southern regions.

Saudi authorities say at least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi drone and missile attacks in the kingdom since September 23. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International airport, the East-West pipeline, and oil infrastructure in eastern and southern Saudi Arabia. The coalition also said it intercepted several drones launched towards the Yemeni city of Marib.

Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili said government forces made gains against the Houthis in al-Hazm and Madghal districts of al-Jawf as fighting intensified in Marib. He said 321 Houthi leaders were killed or wounded in 723 targeted operations by Saudi-backed forces in Taiz, Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf governorates, and 117 military vehicles used by the Iran-allied rebel group were destroyed. The coalition carried out at least 37 air strikes, 56 drone attacks, and 541 artillery strikes.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the Saudi-led coalition launched 72 air strikes against the Houthis in Saada, Taiz, Lahij and al-Jawf governorates over the past 24 hours. Saree said the Houthis targeted Yemen's Saudi-backed forces in the Kharaz area of Lahij governorate with ballistic missiles. Houthi-affiliated media reported two women and two children injured from artillery shelling by Saudi-backed forces in a residential neighbourhood of the Shuaub district in Sanaa. More than 340,000 people have been displaced since August according to the International Organization for Migration. The US Embassy in Riyadh issued a nationwide security alert on Saturday urging Americans to exercise heightened vigilance, citing increased threat of Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure causing civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions, warning hostilities could spread rapidly.

Coalition conducted 37 air strikes, 56 drone attacks, 541 artillery strikes

cards.spoken: Good morning. The Saudi-led coalition says it shot down two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh early Sunday, just a day after it intercepted two drones over Riyadh and southern areas. Spokesperson Turki al-Maliki made both announcements. Since September, at least 26 people have died in Houthi attacks on the kingdom, including strikes on the capital's airport and oil facilities. The coalition also stopped several drones headed for the Yemeni city of Marib. Meanwhile, heavy fighting rages across several Yemeni governorates. Government forces claim gains in al-Jawf and say they've killed or wounded 321 Houthi leaders and destroyed 117 vehicles. The coalition carried out dozens of air and drone strikes and hundreds of artillery rounds. The Houthis say they faced 72 air strikes in the past day and fired missiles at government troops in Lahij. Houthi media report two women and two children hurt by shelling in Sanaa. Over 340,000 people have fled their homes since August. The US Embassy in Riyadh has warned Americans to stay alert, saying Houthi attacks on airports have caused casualties and travel chaos, and the conflict could spread quickly.
